Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, central abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting; features most consistent with acute gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery diarrhoea for 3 days, requiring very frequent toilet visits; associated central lower abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting this morning.  
• Symptom details: Pain localised under umbilicus, mildly relieved after bowel motions; mild tenderness when self-palpated; no radiation. No blood in stool; initially unsure about blood in vomitus but concluded none (strawberry content). Reports some sweating but no documented fever. Possible reduced oral intake and fluid consumption. No chest pain, no change in baseline asthma control, able to walk/talk.  
• Past medical history: Asthma.  
• Medications: Inhaler (brand unspecified), dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: NKDA.  
• Family history: Father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago.  
• Social / preventive: Currently staying home from work because of symptoms; no alcohol/smoking/travel history discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Findings: Patient-reported mild central abdominal tenderness on self-pressing.

Impression:
Acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely food-borne); low suspicion for bowel malignancy given acute presentation.

Plan:
• Advise liberal oral fluids to prevent dehydration.  
• Monitor for fever, worsening abdominal pain, bloody stool/vomit, or inability to keep fluids down.  
• Avoid antibiotics at this stage.  
• Remain off work until symptoms improve.  
• If symptoms worsen or persist >1–2 days, arrange in-person GP review for abdominal examination and further work-up given family history of bowel cancer.  
• Patient agreed with plan and had no further questions.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected: Full medication list, detailed asthma control and inhaler name/dose, travel/diet history, recent vital signs, allergy confirmation, vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: 1) Date of birth: patient variously stated 1992, 1990, and age 48 years (numeric conflict noted). 2) Initially thought blood in vomit, later stated none.  
● Transcript quality: Generally understandable; occasional stutters/inaudible segments but clinical content mostly clear.
